questions.question: What can gloves do?

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your motorcycle's handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: In normal riding conditions, what is the safe following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: When riding behind another vehicle in normal conditions, keep a safe distance of at least two seconds. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you rely on others to find hazards.
It requires you to go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react and have room to move if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially when riding at night. Bright clothing with reflective materials makes you easier for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding a new motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of these do you NOT need to check before riding?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light works

questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and make sure all lights work properly. Paint scratches do not affect safety.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely
Clothing that covers your arms but leaves your legs exposed
Clothing that covers your legs but leaves your arms exposed
Whatever is most comfortable, no matter the safety risk

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs to protect yourself while riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Do not allow a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best thing you can do to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves. Sandals do not provide protection.

questions.question: About how much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, your body eliminates the alcohol from about one drink per hour.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share the lane.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you safely. Change lanes and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up only makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders. It must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason to end the motorcycle skills test?
questions.explanation: The test ends if you drop the motorcycle, tip over, stall the engine four times, do something unsafe, ignore instructions, break a traffic law, or get enough points to fail.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not completely remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not completely remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour, but this varies by person. It is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, you should ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It increases your line of sight.
It decreases your line of sight.
It makes it hard to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows down a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not activate the brake lights.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol levels or make you sober. They may help keep you awake, but nothing changes your blood alcohol level except time.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part closest to the shoulder.
In the part where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror, usually in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors, so this position keeps you visible.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and end up in another lane or off the road. Always turn carefully and at a safe speed.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle can be much more serious than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface ahead?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle a little to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What is the single most effective way to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your chance of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Only for riders with a license less than one year old.

questions.explanation: In Maryland, all motorcycle riders must wear a helmet that meets federal safety standards. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injury in an accident.
